input.brief: Premium Vietnamese movie streaming website using YouTube sources, cinematic posters, and a focused watch flow

direction.name: Dressed as something else
direction.idea: Art-direct the subject as if it belonged to a different, more vivid category. A money app is sold like a streetwear drop. An industrial roaster is presented like a design object. Drilling hardware gets the calm of a watch brand. A parcel-locker service becomes a fairground of stickers. Choose the borrowed category by asking what feeling the audience is missing from this kind of product (swagger, calm, glamour, play) and which category owns that feeling. Then take its manners completely: its type, its pacing, its way of photographing things. The contrast between dull subject and vivid dress is what people remember.
direction.composition: Depends on the borrowed category, so decide it explicitly and write it in your notes. Fashion drop: one shouted condensed headline across the full width, a single cropped image under it, then product facts as a blunt list. Watch or perfume: a centred object on a dark field, a small serif name, very few words, long vertical pauses. Poster or zine: flat colour blocks, heavy type, tilted cut-out images. Museum: one item per screen on a plinth-like band of colour with a short label beside it. Whichever you choose, the page structure stays simple (four to six sections) and every section uses the borrowed manners, including pricing and the footer.
direction.typography: The borrowed category's type, fully committed: condensed and loud, or refined and small. No halfway.
direction.colour: The borrowed category's palette, which will be unlike the subject's sector norm. That mismatch is intended.
direction.imagery: Photograph the subject the way the borrowed category would be photographed. With the dealt set, choose images for attitude, not literal relevance, and crop them hard.
direction.richness: Attitude. The page has a recognisable voice from another world, applied to a subject nobody expected it for.
direction.pitfalls: Name the borrowed category in one word before you start, or the result is merely loud. The content must still be clear: what it is, what it costs, how to get it. Avoid borrowing from 'tech startup', which is the default you are escaping.

hero.name: Counter object, wide wordmark
hero.blueprint: Borrowed from a watch or perfume counter. One flat charcoal field. Centred slightly above the midline, a single low-key photograph of the object about 31% of the viewport wide (columns 5-8), 4:5, its own dark background matched to the field with filter: brightness(0.9) so it sits without a frame. Under it the name runs on one line as an ultra-wide wordmark spanning 72% of the width yet only about 45px tall: an extended face with letter-spacing near 0.6em, or a regular face stretched with transform: scaleX(2.4). Then one centred serif sentence at clamp(24px, 2.6vw, 38px). Then a single centred row at 15px with 48px between its three parts: one specification, the price inside the one solid light rectangle that is also the action, a second specification. The wordmark repeats small top-left and one text link sits top-right, both on 32px margins. The bottom fifth and both outer quarters of the screen stay empty and dark.
hero.mobile: The photograph grows to 70% of the width at 4:5, its top at 16% of the height. The wide wordmark spans the full width inside 20px margins at about 28px tall. The serif sentence sets at 6vw on two lines. The row stacks into three centred lines with the action in the middle at full width. The lowest sixth of the screen stays dark and empty.
hero.headline: The name as a very wide, very low wordmark on one line (up to 12 characters); the serif sentence beneath is the supporting line, up to 40 characters.

type.note: A true didone with hairline serifs and vertical stress over a light geometric sans, the classic fashion-magazine pairing. Suits luxury property, jewellery, fragrance and fashion.

palette.name: Report blocks
palette.note: A white base with flat blocks of orange, sage, acid yellow and black assigned to whole modules: figure tiles, quote panels and chapter bands. Text is black on every colour and off-white on black, and orange is also the button colour.

motion.name: Slow crossfade
motion.description: The principal photograph quietly changes: three or four images of the same framing crossfade over about 1.6 seconds, holding five to six seconds each, or the fixed image changes when its matching section arrives. It should feel like light shifting in a room. Pause when the tab is hidden; under reduced motion show only the first image.

sections.name: Object riding down the schedule
sections.blueprint: A schedule of dated events (races, concerts, tastings, departures) with the subject's own object travelling down it. On a dark flat ground, on the page's own margins, the heading is one centred line of condensed capitals at clamp(40px, 3.6vw, 56px), split into its two words with a gap between them, and in the gap stands a cut-out photograph of the object seen from above or in profile, about 320px wide (22% of the width) and up to 64% of the viewport tall. Below come full-width rows 84px tall, each a two-part grid: the event's name at 26px in condensed capitals on the left with a one-line note at 16px in the soft ink under it, and the date and place right-aligned at 16px on the note's baseline. Rows alternate between the ground and a tone one step lighter instead of rules. As the page scrolls, the object leaves the heading and moves down the centre line over the rows (`position: sticky` in a centred column that spans the list, `pointer-events: none`), where it covers only the empty middle of each row and marks how far the reader has come. The row for the next event takes the accent colour across its whole band, with its name and date in the accent's ink. About ten rows fit on one screen; the list ends 120px under the last row.
sections.mobile: Rows stack at full width on 20px margins: the name at 22px on up to two lines, the note at 16px, the date under the note. The object shrinks to 40% of the width and stays in the heading; it does not travel, because on a phone it would cover the rows. The accent band stays on the next event.

sections.name: Two giant words compared
sections.blueprint: No photographs: the thing shown is a pair of words, characters or figures that make the point by comparison (before and after, input and output, ours and the usual). At the top of the section, on one row: the heading, two to four words at 28–36px, at the left margin, and a paragraph of up to 60 words at 17px starting at column 7. Then 12vh of space. Below, two specimens side by side, one starting on column 1 and one on column 7, each set at clamp(180px, 34vw, 520px) with leading 0.8, so each fills about half the viewport's width. The section has a fixed height and overflow: hidden, so its bottom edge cuts both specimens at roughly 60% of their height. One short caption at 16px sits above the top-left of each specimen, naming it. Both specimens share one ink; the difference is in the letterforms or values, not in colour.
sections.mobile: Heading first, then the paragraph, at full width. The two specimens stack, each at 62vw type size in its own 38svh box with overflow hidden so the lower part is cut. Captions sit above each box at 15px. The second box takes the inverse colours of the first.

sections.name: Inset panel, shaped portrait
sections.blueprint: A deep-toned panel inset 20px from the page edges with a 12px radius, about 110svh tall, `overflow: hidden`. Left half: a two-line statement of four to seven words at clamp(40px, 4.4vw, 64px) in a pale ink, top-left with 56px padding; it is the heading and has nothing above it. Below it a photograph of the person or the workshop, masked with `clip-path` or an SVG `mask` to one bold shape taken from the subject (a four-lobed flower, a circle, an arch, a chamfered block), 38vw across, positioned so the panel's bottom edge crops its lowest fifth. Right side, starting at 63% of the width and 56px from the top: two text blocks 300px wide and 64px apart, each a subhead at 22px over a four-line paragraph at 15px; then one solid button in the accent colour. Between the statement and the text blocks the panel is empty. One photograph only.
sections.mobile: The panel is inset 10px and stacks: the statement at 8.5vw, then the two text blocks at full width, the button, and last the shaped photograph at 86vw across, centred and cropped by the panel's bottom edge by a quarter of its height.

sections.name: Contact as the headline
sections.blueprint: A full-bleed field in one saturated palette colour, at least 90svh tall. Top row, 40px from the edge: two or three short notes at 15px in columns 1–7 (address, hours, a one-line description) and a back-to-top text link at the right margin. Then a tall empty gap. In the lower half, the way to get in touch is the display line: the telephone number or the email address itself, set at 8–9vw, flush left, hard against the margin, as one link. An email address may break once, before the @, giving two lines. Size it with `clamp()` so the longest line fills at least 80% of the width. Under it, one row of small text at 14px spread across three positions: links at the left, credits in the centre, city and year at the right. The wordmark appears only small, in the top row.
sections.mobile: Notes stack at the top at 15px. The contact line sits in the lower half at 12vw; a telephone number stays on one line, an email breaks before the @ and is sized so each half fits the width. The meta row becomes three stacked lines at 13px.

references.name: Locker Land
references.idea: A dry B2B parcel-locker pitch dressed as a fairground of die-cut stickers, where the main navigation is a fan of five tilted illustrated cards.
references.hero: Post-red field overlaid with a faint lighter-red square grid. Small white brand lock-up top-left; a white pill button with a hard dark-red offset shadow top-right. Top-centre, a two-line sticker-style logo (cream letters, thick cream outline, small locker drawing) about 20% of viewport width. Beneath it a two-line centred white sentence at 18px; no larger headline. The lower half is a fan of five portrait cards with thick coloured frames and rounded corners: centre card upright, neighbours rotated about 8 degrees, the outer pair about 18 degrees and cropped by the viewport edges, each with a label tab overlapping its bottom edge. A two-line caption sits centred below.
references.type: apDisplay, a brand grotesque, is the only family: weight 500, sentence case, slightly tight. Body 16-18px; section headings in dark red reach about 5.9vw. The hero has no typographic headline, the sticker logo plays that role. Labels inside sticker tabs go bold.
references.colour: #dc1928 #fdf3db #952625 #e0a912 #5b7a94 #d46831 — Post red and cream alternate as full section fields; mustard, slate blue, burnt orange and maroon are reserved for card frames and badges. Warm, flat, no gradients.
references.imagery: Flat vector drawings (parcel, locker, hand holding a card) with thick cream die-cut outlines and hard offset shadows, plus candid photos of people at lockers placed inside arch-shaped cut-outs and wide rounded video tiles.
references.layout: Every section is a centre-stacked composition on a full-width colour field, with a pill-shaped sticky sub-nav top-centre after the hero. Sections are separated by ornament rather than whitespace: a red and cream checkerboard strip, a scalloped awning edge. Cards come in tilted rows of three or five.

sections.description: On red beneath a checkerboard strip, a dark-red pill with a dotted inner border holds the heading. Three statistics are scattered as tilted stickers instead of a row: a mustard circle, a maroon starburst seal with a cursor-arrow sticker overlapping it, and a slate-blue tag shape, each with a small parcel or locker illustration tucked onto a corner. Figures are large; captions are tiny and centred inside each shape.

On cream, the heading sits in a white rounded box with dark-red outline and offset shadow, hanging directly under the sticky nav. Below, three equal portrait cards in mustard, slate blue and orange, each with a dark-red border and hard offset shadow, containing an arch-shaped photo cut-out of people, a tilted name-tag sticker, a starburst date badge, two centred lines of copy and a small white pill button.

A centred locker illustration with icon stickers orbiting it, a centred heading and two-line intro, then a full-width two-by-two mosaic of video stills with no gaps and rounded outer corners. Each tile carries one large white rounded chip with a bold red word, placed low and off-centre. A hand-drawn orange arrow sticker overlaps the mosaic's top-left corner, pointing in.

Five stacked white pill-shaped rows in a centred column about 65% of the page wide, each with dark-red outline, hard offset shadow, question at left and chevron at right. A checkerboard strip then returns the page to red, where an oversized version of the sticker logo sits centred with a one-line copyright beneath.

steal: Turn the primary navigation into a fan of tilted illustrated cards in the hero, centre card upright and the outer ones rotated and cropped by the viewport edges.
Give every element the same die-cut sticker treatment (thick cream outline plus a hard, unblurred offset shadow in a darker shade of the background) so buttons, cards and badges read as one family.
Present statistics as differently shaped badges (circle, starburst, tag) scattered at angles rather than as three equal columns.

references.name: Moto Finance
references.idea: A metal card presented like a museum piece: lit by a single overhead light box in a black room, then orbiting through dim architectural stills.
references.hero: Black full-bleed 3D scene. A pale silver-lavender light panel, a trapezoid in perspective like a ceiling light box, occupies the top 20% and centre 55% of the viewport. The two-line uppercase headline, centred at 4.4vw in medium grotesk with tight leading, straddles the panel's lower edge so its first line sits half on light, half on black. In the exact centre a small metal card stands on a low plinth, only about 150px wide, surrounded by darkness. A light-grey pill button (about 250 by 52px) is centred near the bottom; the logo is top-left and a dark pill button top-right.
references.type: Neue Montreal only: weight 500 uppercase at 64px (4.4vw) with near-zero tracking and leading under 1.0 for headings, 20px sentence case for body, tiny caps labels in the footer. Three sizes; centred until the left-aligned footer.
references.colour: #080808 #edefef #c4cbd6 #e1e5e5 #2a2f3a — Black with cool silver-grey and no brand colour at all. One section inverts to pale grey-white with grey type; the only chroma is amber city lights and a blue atmosphere rim on the globe.
references.imagery: Rendered chrome card with an embossed profile medallion, a night-side Earth, and small dim architectural and fashion stills floating as tilted panels in 3D. Everything underexposed, cool and low-saturation.
references.layout: Full-viewport scenes stacked one per screen, each with a centred uppercase heading, an optional short sub-line and a pill button. One light interlude breaks the black. The footer switches to a left-aligned statement with link columns at the far right.

sections.description: Centred heading at the top with a two-line grey sub-line and a pale pill button directly under it. The lower 45% is the top arc of a night-side Earth rising from the bottom edge, about 75% of the viewport wide, with city lights and a bright blue-white rim on the upper right. Three small dark capsule labels with check icons float over and beside the globe at staggered positions, like status notifications.

A dark 3D room: about twelve small photo panels (roughly 70 by 90px, each tilted at its own angle, heavily dimmed) arranged in two loose rows across the full width, receding with blur. The card stands edge-on in the centre, much larger, catching a specular highlight. Later the card faces front at top-centre and a centred two-line heading with a pill button sits under it.

A pale grey-white band. Two tall columns of currency amounts in mid-size light-grey sans, one at a quarter and one at three-quarters of the width, each fading to white at top and bottom like slot-machine reels, with the centre rows darkest. Between them, three short centred lines of small black text. The bottom edge of the band reveals a dark photograph.

steal: Let a headline straddle the edge of a light shape so one line is half on light and half on dark.
Show the product very small in a large dark space in the first viewport, then let it grow as the page scrolls.
Use vertically scrolling columns of real-looking figures, faded at both ends, as a quiet backdrop for a three-line statement.
references.media: An 11s hero video of a CG metal card on a plinth covers the whole first screen and holds on its last frame. Then a pinned WebGL globe in the lower half under centred text, a 3D card centred in a depth cloud of small photo tiles dimmed to 30-40%, full-bleed sticky photographs with text docked in opposite corners, and a photo strip sitting on an index list; all low-key and desaturated, photos meeting the near-black ground through 200-300px fades, 0px radius.
references.motion: The intro ends in about 1.2s as the camera pushes in and the headline, nav and button arrive (load 9.9s), and Lenis then runs 32 ScrollTriggers: the globe pins for 2.5 viewports at scrub 1, the card turns in 3D across its section, the theme inverts to pale grey with the nav colour following, and benefit rows scrub in one by one. Lines rise by yPercent over 0.65s power3.out and leave over 0.45s power2.in, and headings rise from a blur over 1s power2.inOut.

references.name: The state of the gallery
references.idea: A year-in-review told as a flight over a glowing particle landscape, where each statistic or pick is a single word floating in 3D space.
references.hero: The desktop capture caught the loader: a blue-black screen with a faint dot grid, a 4px acid-yellow progress bar across the top edge, the small logo centred at the top, and a percentage counter at 13.9vw (200px) in thin pale blue-grey grotesk anchored bottom-left. The loaded hero, seen on mobile, splits the title in two: the first two words top-left and the last three bottom-right at the same giant size, with a centred uppercase paragraph between them, all over a full-bleed terrain of olive-green haze and yellow particles. Tiny capital labels occupy all four corners.
references.type: Overused Grotesk only, regular weight: display words at 5 to 14vw in pale blue-grey with a faint lilac sheen, small parenthesised counts set as superscripts beside them, and 10px uppercase captions and corner labels. Two sizes and no bold.
references.colour: #08090d #515721 #b9c6cd #e6f21a #c8b9ee — Blue-black ground; the olive-to-acid-yellow glow of the particle field is the single colour. Type is cool pale grey with a lilac tint, and the yellow loader bar is the brightest element.
references.imagery: A procedural landscape of soft olive fog ridges with thousands of yellow-white points streaming toward the horizon in perspective; later, a curved floor of small tilted white tiles standing for catalogued sites. No photographs.
references.layout: One pinned canvas with a text overlay. Four corner labels stay fixed; each scroll step puts a single word or name at the centre with a one-line caption beneath it in the lower third. Nothing else appears on screen.

sections.description: Full-bleed particle terrain. One category word is centred at about 5vw in pale iridescent grotesk, with its count in parentheses set small and raised at the word's top-right like a superscript. A single-line uppercase caption at 10px sits centred roughly 20% below. Behind the word the particles briefly cluster into the shape of a large numeral. Corner labels are unchanged.

A top-pick slide: a tiny uppercase label above, then the pick's name centred at about 5vw and partly occluded by the scene. Below it dozens of small white rectangular tiles lie on a curved, receding floor grid, some flat and some tilting up toward the camera, growing larger toward the bottom edge of the viewport. A one-line caption sits under the name.

steal: Split a title in two and pin the halves to opposite corners, top-left and bottom-right, at the same giant size with the supporting paragraph centred between them.
Attach a count to a big word as a small parenthesised superscript at its top-right instead of building a stat card.
Make the loading percentage the first giant typographic element, anchored bottom-left under a full-width accent progress bar.
references.media: One fixed WebGL canvas is the only surface: a particle landscape covers 99% of the first screen with the title straight on it, and as you travel the particles leave the ground to form numerals, a figure, floating screenshot cards and a tile-grid panel, while streams of thumbnail tiles fly low between beats. No img or video elements.
references.motion: A percentage preloader is still at 89% at 4.5s, though the load event fired at 2.1s; after it the wheel is captured, each step easing the camera forward to the next beat, with text-free fly-through steps between them (5 of 13 screens show only terrain). Characters rise with a stagger, transform and opacity over 0.7s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1) on 704 spans, 0.42s for secondary lines, and counts pop in with an overshoot from 0.6 to 1.08 to 1.
